### Hey there!

My name is Lauren and I'm a Ph.D. candidate in the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at UCLA, where I study how species-specific differences in dispersal influence community assembly & biodiversity in a model annual grassland. My ongoing projects combine field experiments, functional trait data, and mechanistic modeling to explore variation in dispersal among species and determine how plant communites are shaped by feedbacks between the environment, plant performance, and dispersal.

Prior to my graduate research, I earned my B.S. in Plant Biology from UC Davis with minors in Professional Writing and Ecology, Evolution, & Biodiversity. There, I also completed my California Naturalist certification, which kickstarted my love for community science. You can find me documenting every organism I see on iNaturalist, eBird, or a number of other community science platforms.
